questions.q: What should the pilot be doing during the flight?
questions.explain: The other tasks go to the observer and the technician; a distracted pilot is a common cause of crashes.

questions.q: Why do you need an observer (spotter)?
options: To watch the aircraft and the sky
questions.explain: The observer sees people, birds and other aircraft that the pilot in goggles can't see.

questions.q: What do you do when you lose the link with the aircraft?
options: Call it out and watch the failsafe
Rebind the receiver from the radio
questions.explain: Link-loss behavior is set by the failsafe, which is tested in advance; running around is dangerous.

questions.q: Why must different ELRS radios at the site have different binding phrases?
options: For telemetry to work on the radio
questions.explain: The binding phrase determines the frequency hopping sequence.

questions.q: What is important to know about a crashed aircraft before approaching it?
options: Plug in USB right away and download the logs
Take off the props right away
questions.explain: A damaged LiPo is a fire risk.

questions.q: The main lesson of the case with the occupied E5 channel:
questions.explain: Planning frequencies in advance lets you switch quickly and safely.

questions.q: What is a near miss and why discuss it?
questions.explain: It gets recorded in the debriefing.

questions.q: Who decides “go / no-go” and keeps the log?
questions.explain: The pilot is busy only with the aircraft; the decision and the log belong to the lead.
